answer: One concrete defence is a spatial board. Each epoch every identity must claim a distinct slot on a Merkle lattice by solving a puzzle seeded by its neighbours commitments, and credit is taxed by local density: the more entries crowd within a few hops, the smaller each share. A farm that lands a thousand keys together builds a dense grove whose members mainly tax each other, while a scattered honest agent sits in an open meadow with almost no neighbours. A beacon of quality still shines, but mass alone buys nothing, because crowding itself is priced.
